notes: BATCH J (insulins). SOURCES: emc SmPCs only for the products; MHRA Products search index (the JSON index behind products.mhra.gov.uk) used only to confirm absence of products. NO UK PRODUCT: insulin glargine/lixisenatide (clinic trade name and EU spelling searched on emc, ingredient searched on emc; no MHRA Products document has lixisenatide as an active substance) -> availability no-uk-product, no rules. SUBSTITUTE SmPCs: (1) insulin degludec 100 units/mL pre-filled pen: no UK SmPC found on emc or MHRA Products (only the 100 units/mL cartridge and 200 units/mL pen); the 100 units/mL cartridge SmPC (emc-2944) is used and this is stated in the formulation note. (2) Human biphasic 30/70: the clinic's second 30/70 brand has no UK SmPC on emc or MHRA Products; the other brand's 30/70 vial SmPC (emc-8193) is used. The clinic monograph link emc-3849 is the soluble human insulin vial (not a 30/70 product). FORMULATIONS kept distinct: lispro solution vs biphasic 50/50 vs 25/75 (clinic calls it 75/25); aspart solution vs biphasic 30/70; glargine 100 units/mL pen, 100 units/mL vial, 300 units/mL pen (not bioequivalent, switching rules stated); human soluble vs isophane vs biphasic 30/70. CONFLICTS BETWEEN UK SOURCES: (a) Hypoglycaemia: section 4.3 contraindication in the Lilly analogue and Lilly human insulin SmPCs; Novo Nordisk SmPCs put it in 4.4 as "must not be injected"; both mapped to contraindicated (mapping table: "must not be"). Sanofi glargine and Novo degludec SmPCs have no such statement, so no hypoglycaemia rule for those. (b) Human insulin paediatrics: Novo soluble/isophane SmPCs say they can be used in children and adolescents; Lilly human insulin SmPCs say no paediatric data. Kept as one item naming both; no age rule. (c) Human insulin hypersensitivity: Lilly 4.3 adds "unless used as part of a desensitisation programme". (d) Interaction lists differ by manufacturer (e.g. Lilly names ARBs, SSRIs, captopril; Novo names sulfonamides, sympathomimetics, oral contraceptives; Sanofi names fibrates, fluoxetine, diuretics, oestrogens/progestogens). Each rule cites the SmPC(s) that name it. INTERACTION LEVELS follow each SmPC's wording: Lilly ("The physician should be consulted") -> caution; Sanofi ("may require dose adjustment of insulin glargine") -> dose; Novo (no action stated, only "may reduce/increase insulin requirement") -> info. Glucose-lowering interactions carry effect hypoglycaemia; glucose-raising ones have no effect tag (no hyperglycaemia effect exists) and share the concern text "Reduced glucose-lowering effect of insulin" so they merge per pair. Where an SmPC names a master medicine inside a class (aspirin within salicylates; salbutamol within beta2 stimulants/sympathomimetics) both a group rule and a medicine rule were added with the same concern/effect so the engine merges them. GLP-1 receptor agonists: dose rule for biphasic aspart and degludec (SmPC 20% reduction), monitor rule elsewhere (MHRA DSU 2019, reused source id mhra-dsu-glp1-dka-insulin-2019). Oral contraceptives (no master group) are expressed as condition rules on hormonal-contraception (condition defined in batch D). GROUPS: insulin + antidiabetic memberships for the five UK insulin entries quoted from SmPC 5.1. Groups this batch relies on that must be populated by other batches: oral-antidiabetic, glp1-agonist, beta-blocker, ace-inhibitor, arb, salicylate, sulfonamide, maoi, ssri, corticosteroid, thyroid-hormone, thiazide, diuretic, sympathomimetic, beta2-agonist, fibrate, progestogen. NEW CONDITION: hypoglycaemia. Renal: no SmPC gives an eGFR/CrCl threshold for any insulin, so renal effects are condition rules on renal-impairment (defined in batch G), not numeric renal rules. NOT VERIFIABLE: insulin glargine SmPC 4.8 table frequencies other than hypoglycaemia (table columns are lost in the fetched text; stated as such). Insulin lispro 4.8 table columns also lost; frequencies used only where the prose states them (local allergy common, systemic allergy rare). BRAND PRESCRIBING: SPS (citing NICE) says insulins should be prescribed by brand name and device; SPS insulin confusion page says brand name alone is insufficient where a brand has several strengths/devices. MHRA DSU 2015 (high strength/biosimilar insulins) gives switching and monitoring advice but does not itself say "prescribe by brand". BNF not accessed (geo-blocked). AUDIT 2026-10-17 (independent check, see scripts/medcheck-uk/audit/J-K.md): the 100 units/mL insulin degludec pre-filled pen DOES have a UK SmPC on MHRA Products (PLGB 04668/0410, source mhra-plgb04668-0410-spc); the substitute-SmPC note above is superseded. The pen SmPC is now the formulation source; clinical quotes still cite the newer cartridge SmPC (64 of 68 quotes checked word-for-word in the pen SmPC; the 4 others differ only by table layout or pen storage). Glargine DKA rule reworded (treatment of DKA, not a ban on basal insulin). Premixed lispro and biphasic aspart IV warnings moved from contraindications (4.3) to cautions (they are 4.2/4.4 statements).
